html:
In June 1873 Sultan Barghash bin Said of Zanzibar signed a treaty with Britain that closed the public slave market of Zanzibar town and banned the sea trade in slaves from the East African coast.

Zanzibar was the hub of the East African slave trade. Captives from the interior were sold there to work on the island's clove plantations or shipped to Arabia and the Persian Gulf. Reports by David Livingstone stirred British opinion, and Britain threatened a naval blockade to force the sultan's hand.

The Anglican Universities' Mission to Central Africa bought the market site and built Christ Church Cathedral on it, finished in 1880. Its altar is said to stand where the whipping post stood. The trade went on by land and in secret for years, and slavery itself was not abolished in Zanzibar until 1897. The same year, 1873, Russia forced the closing of the Khiva slave market in Central Asia.
sum: In June 1873 Sultan Barghash bin Said of Zanzibar signed a treaty with Britain that closed the public slave market of Zanzibar town and banned the sea trade in slaves from the East African coast.
